decisions.rationale: Lead Manectric + Talonflame pressures the expected rain opener with Lightning Rod protection and priority Tailwind/Taunt. Mega Floette provides immediate Water/Ground pressure and broad Fairy damage, while Hatterene supplies a durable Trick Room pivot if rain speed control becomes problematic.
decisions.notebook: Preferred rain matchup structure: lead Manectric + Talonflame for Lightning Rod and priority speed-control disruption; retain Mega Floette as the main breaker with Energy Ball into Swampert and Fairy pressure into Basculegion, Whimsicott, and Ampharos. Hatterene is the primary alternate Trick Room mode versus Swift Swim.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper and Swampert lead to set up Drizzle rain and immediate offensive pressure, backed by choice-scarfed Basculegion and fast Prankster Whimsicott in the back to clean up and maintain speed control.
decisions.notebook: Maintain rain offense core with Pelipper + Mega Swampert leads and Basculegion/Whimsicott backline for game 1.

decisions.rationale: Gale Wings Tailwind establishes speed control before either foe can act, while Life Orb Thunderbolt is a guaranteed OHKO on Pelipper if it stays in. This removes rain support immediately and leaves Tailwind to offset Mega Swampert’s Swift Swim.
decisions.notebook: Against rain leads, prioritize Gale Wings Tailwind plus immediate Electric pressure on Pelipper; preserve Floette-Eternal for Energy Ball into Swampert and Fairy damage into Water/Fairy or Grass/Fairy reserves, with Hatterene retained as a Trick Room pivot against Swift Swim.

decisions.rationale: Protect on both Pelipper and Swampert on turn 1 is the safest play against Manectric and Gale Wings Talonflame, wasting Talonflame's Gale Wings and protecting against potential double-targeting while allowing Swampert to Mega Evolve safely.
decisions.notebook: Rain core active: Pelipper and Mega Swampert leads with Basculegion and Whimsicott in reserve. Watch out for Talonflame's Gale Wings and Manectric's Lightning Rod.

decisions.rationale: Refresh Tailwind with Gale Wings while Manectric secures the guaranteed Thunderbolt KO on Pelipper; this accepts Swampert’s likely Earthquake KO on Manectric but removes rain support and preserves a fast Floette-Eternal answer to Swampert.
decisions.notebook: Against rain, use Gale Wings Tailwind and immediate Electric pressure to remove Pelipper when possible. Floette-Eternal is the primary preserved answer to Swampert via Energy Ball; retain Hatterene as a Trick Room pivot versus Swift Swim.

decisions.rationale: Floette-Eternal preserves immediate Tailwind-boosted Energy Ball pressure into Mega Swampert while avoiding the much worse Ground matchup Hatterene would face.
decisions.notebook: Against rain, prioritize Gale Wings Tailwind and Electric pressure to remove Pelipper. Preserve Floette-Eternal as the primary Mega Swampert answer with Energy Ball; retain Hatterene as a Trick Room pivot against Swift Swim.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper targets Talonflame with Hydro Pump (guaranteed OHKO on Focus Sash due to breaking it or damage overkill, or Talonflame may be vulnerable since Pelipper protected last turn and Tailwind is up). Swampert Mega Evolves and uses Waterfall on Manectric to guarantee a kill while avoiding hitting its own partner with Earthquake (since Talonflame is immune/flying and Manectric is targeted by Waterfall).

Pelipper fainted last turn, so we bring in Basculegion under rain, while Mega Swampert passes its turn to make the substitution. Basculegion outspeeds and threatens the remaining opponents with its Swift Swim/Choice Scarf speed under rain, and Tailwind is active for the foe.
decisions.notebook: Rain core is rolling with Mega Swampert and Basculegion in reserve; watch out for remaining backline threats (Floette-Eternal, Hatterene, Scrafty, Goodra-Hisui) and Talonflame.

decisions.rationale: Mega Energy Ball maximizes the chance to remove Mega Swampert immediately while priority Brave Bird puts decisive chip on Basculegion for Talonflame’s next priority attack.
decisions.notebook: Against rain, preserve or use Floette-Eternal’s Grass pressure to remove Mega Swampert; Talonflame’s Gale Wings Brave Bird can chip or finish faster threats before they move. Hatterene remains the Trick Room pivot if it can enter safely.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Talonflame is under Tailwind and holds Focus Sash, but Basculegion's Wave Crash and Mega Swampert's Waterfall both target Talonflame to break through its Sash and remove its offensive pressure immediately.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper fainted; rain has 6 turns remaining. Swampert-Mega and Basculegion pressure backline threats with rain-boosted Water attacks while Whimsicott sits safely in reserve.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Floette outspeeds both foes while Tailwind is active and Energy Ball cleanly removes the 17% Basculegion before its Choice-locked Wave Crash. Hatterene’s Dazzling Gleam pressures Whimsicott through Focus Sash while also providing backup damage.
decisions.notebook: Against this rain composition, preserve Floette’s Grass pressure for Swampert and use Hatterene’s Trick Room only when slower opposing attackers remain threatening. Whimsicott carries Prankster Tailwind and Encore with Focus Sash; Basculegion is Choice Scarf Adaptability and can be locked into Wave Crash.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion is Choice-locked into Wave Crash and can hit Hatterene for a guaranteed OHKO. Whimsicott sets up Tailwind to seize speed control as the opponent's Tailwind expires this turn.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion is Choice-locked into Wave Crash. Whimsicott provides crucial Tailwind support to outspeed opposing threats post-Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast is Floette-Mega’s strongest available attack into Whimsicott and avoids voluntarily selecting the previously used Energy Ball.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Whimsicott is Prankster Focus Sash with Tailwind, Encore, Moonblast, and Protect. Basculegion is Choice Scarf Adaptability and was revealed locked into Wave Crash after using it. Floette-Mega’s Fairy Aura boosts its Fairy attacks.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion is fainted so it passes. Whimsicott uses Moonblast against the sole remaining active threat, Floette-Mega.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Mega is the only remaining opposing Pokémon in Game 1. Whimsicott outspeeds under Tailwind and deals special Fairy damage with Moonblast.

reflections.summary: Won by correctly prioritizing Pelipper and Mega Swampert, removing rain’s setter and its main rain abuser while Mega Floette cleaned the weakened remaining core. The 4-Pokémon bring—Manectric, Talonflame, Hatterene, and Floette—fit well into rain, and Mega Floette was the appropriate evolution; piloting had no recorded errors.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, preserve Talonflame or Hatterene more carefully once the rain core is removed, since either can provide a stronger endgame speed-control option than trading both into Basculegion’s Wave Crash.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favors Pelipper + Mega Swampert rain leads and brought Basculegion plus Whimsicott behind them in Game 1. Pelipper is Damp Rock Drizzle with Hurricane, Hydro Pump, Protect, and Tailwind. Mega Swampert is Adamant with Earthquake, Waterfall, Ice Punch, and Protect. Whimsicott is Prankster Focus Sash with Tailwind, Encore, Moonblast, and Protect. Basculegion is Adamant Choice Scarf Adaptability with Last Respects, Wave Crash, Flip Turn, and Aqua Jet; after selecting Wave Crash it is locked into it. Prioritize removing Pelipper and Mega Swampert; Mega Floette’s Energy Ball and Fairy Aura-boosted Fairy damage match well into this composition. Respect Whimsicott Tailwind/Sash and Basculegion’s Choice Scarf Wave Crash endgame.

reflections.summary: The opponent established speed control via Talonflame's Tailwind and leveraged Mega Floette's Fairy Aura-boosted coverage alongside backline threats to overwhelm the Swift Swim setup and dismantle the rain core.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Whimsicott initially to block or counter opposing speed control immediately and better position Swampert and Basculegion for uncontested offensive pressure.
reflections.notebook: Opponent brings Talonflame with Tailwind and Focus Sash, Manectric with Life Orb and Thunderbolt, Hatterene with Sitrus Berry, and Mega Floette with Fairy Aura. Goodra-Hisui and Scrafty were left in the back for Game 1.
